events.title: First Moving Image Captured
events.description: Eadweard Muybridge uses a series of cameras to capture a horse in motion, proving all four hooves leave the ground.

events.title: Roundhay Garden Scene
events.description: Louis Le Prince films the oldest surviving motion picture in Leeds, England.

events.title: Kinetoscope Patented
events.description: Thomas Edison patents the Kinetoscope, an early motion picture exhibition device.

events.title: First Public Lumière Screening
events.description: The Lumière brothers hold the first public screening of ten short films at the Grand Café in Paris.

events.title: A Trip to the Moon Released
events.description: Georges Méliès releases 'Le Voyage dans la lune', pioneering special effects and narrative storytelling.

events.title: The Great Train Robbery Released
events.description: Edwin S. Porter's landmark Western introduces cross-cutting and on-location filming.

events.title: First Nickelodeon Opens
events.description: The first Nickelodeon theater opens in Pittsburgh, making movies accessible to the masses for five cents.

events.title: The Birth of a Nation Released
events.description: D.W. Griffith's controversial epic revolutionizes film technique but is criticized for its racist content.

events.title: Technicolor Corporation Founded
events.description: The Technicolor Motion Picture Corporation is founded, eventually dominating the color film industry.

events.title: Charlie Chaplin's 'The Tramp' Debuts
events.description: Chaplin introduces his iconic 'Little Tramp' character in the film 'The Tramp'.

events.title: Intolerance Released
events.description: D.W. Griffith releases his ambitious multi-narrative epic as a response to criticisms of his previous work.

events.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari Released
events.description: A landmark of German Expressionist cinema, featuring stylized sets and a twist ending.

events.title: Nanook of the North Released
events.description: Robert J. Flaherty's film is considered the first feature-length documentary.

events.title: Nosferatu Released
events.description: F.W. Murnau's unauthorized adaptation of Dracula becomes a cornerstone of horror cinema.

events.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame Released
events.description: Lon Chaney stars in this massive production, cementing his status as 'The Man of a Thousand Faces'.

events.title: Battleship Potemkin Released
events.description: Sergei Eisenstein's masterpiece introduces revolutionary montage editing techniques.

events.title: The Gold Rush Released
events.description: Charlie Chaplin's comedy epic about the Klondike Gold Rush becomes a massive success.

events.title: Metropolis Released
events.description: Fritz Lang's pioneering sci-fi epic features groundbreaking special effects and social commentary.

events.title: The Jazz Singer Released
events.description: The first feature-length 'talkie' marks the end of the silent era.

events.title: Wings Wins First Best Picture
events.description: At the first Academy Awards, 'Wings' is named Outstanding Picture (Best Picture).

events.title: All Quiet on the Western Front Released
events.description: The powerful anti-war film wins Best Picture at the 3rd Academy Awards.

events.title: Cimarron Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first Western to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.

events.title: Dracula and Frankenstein Released
events.description: Universal Pictures releases two iconic horror films, launching the Universal Monsters era.

events.title: Grand Hotel Wins Best Picture
events.description: The only Best Picture winner to receive no other nominations.

events.title: King Kong Released
events.description: The landmark creature feature showcases Willis O'Brien's stop-motion animation.

events.title: It Happened One Night Wins Big Five
events.description: The first film to win all five major Academy Awards (Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, Screenplay).

events.title: Mutiny on the Bounty Wins Best Picture
events.description: The historical epic starring Clark Gable wins the top prize.

events.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs Released
events.description: Walt Disney releases the first feature-length cel-animated film.

events.title: The Life of Emile Zola Wins Best Picture
events.description: The biographical film about the French writer wins the 10th Academy Award for Best Picture.

events.title: You Can't Take It with You Wins Best Picture
events.description: Frank Capra's comedy wins the top prize at the 11th Academy Awards.

events.title: Gone with the Wind Released
events.description: The epic historical romance wins 10 Oscars and remains the highest-grossing film when adjusted for inflation.

events.title: The Wizard of Oz Released
events.description: The beloved fantasy film showcases vivid Technicolor and becomes a cultural touchstone.

events.title: Rebecca Wins Best Picture
events.description: Alfred Hitchcock's only film to win Best Picture.

events.title: Citizen Kane Released
events.description: Orson Welles' debut is now widely considered the greatest film ever made.

events.title: How Green Was My Valley Wins Best Picture
events.description: John Ford's drama wins Best Picture over Citizen Kane.

events.title: Mrs. Miniver Wins Best Picture
events.description: The wartime drama wins 6 Oscars at the 15th Academy Awards.

events.title: Casablanca Wins Best Picture
events.description: The classic romantic drama starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman wins the top prize.

events.title: Going My Way Wins Best Picture
events.description: The musical comedy-drama starring Bing Crosby wins 7 Oscars.

events.title: The Lost Weekend Wins Best Picture
events.description: Billy Wilder's gritty look at alcoholism wins the top prize.

events.title: The Best Years of Our Lives Wins Best Picture
events.description: A moving look at veterans returning from WWII wins 7 Oscars.

events.title: Gentleman's Agreement Wins Best Picture
events.description: The drama about anti-Semitism wins the top prize at the 20th Academy Awards.

events.title: Hamlet Wins Best Picture
events.description: Laurence Olivier's adaptation is the first British film to win Best Picture.

events.title: All About Eve Wins 6 Oscars
events.description: The film receives a record 14 nominations and wins Best Picture.

events.title: Sunset Boulevard Released
events.description: Billy Wilder's noir masterpiece examines the dark side of Hollywood fame.

events.title: An American in Paris Wins Best Picture
events.description: The vibrant musical starring Gene Kelly wins 6 Oscars.

events.title: The Greatest Show on Earth Wins Best Picture
events.description: Cecil B. DeMille's circus epic wins the top prize at the 25th Academy Awards.

events.title: From Here to Eternity Wins 8 Oscars
events.description: The wartime drama wins Best Picture, tying the record for most wins at the time.

events.title: Seven Samurai Released
events.description: Akira Kurosawa's epic masterpiece redefines action cinema.

events.title: On the Waterfront Wins Best Picture
events.description: Marlon Brando's powerful performance anchors this 8-Oscar winner.

events.title: Marty Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first film based on a teleplay to win Best Picture.

events.title: Around the World in 80 Days Wins Best Picture
events.description: The star-studded adventure wins 5 Oscars at the 29th Academy Awards.

events.title: The Bridge on the River Kwai Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: David Lean's war epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: Gigi Wins 9 Oscars
events.description: The musical sets a new record for most wins for a single film at the time.

events.title: Ben-Hur Wins 11 Oscars
events.description: The massive epic sets a record for most Oscar wins that would not be tied for decades.

events.title: Psycho Released
events.description: Alfred Hitchcock's thriller shocks audiences and changes horror cinema forever.

events.title: The Apartment Wins Best Picture
events.description: Billy Wilder's romantic comedy-drama wins the top prize.

events.title: West Side Story Wins 10 Oscars
events.description: The musical adaptation wins Best Picture.

events.title: Lawrence of Arabia Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: David Lean's biographical epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: Tom Jones Wins Best Picture
events.description: The British adventure comedy wins the top prize at the 36th Academy Awards.

events.title: My Fair Lady Wins 8 Oscars
events.description: The musical starring Audrey Hepburn wins Best Picture.

events.title: The Sound of Music Wins Best Picture
events.description: The beloved musical wins 5 Oscars and becomes a massive commercial hit.

events.title: A Man for All Seasons Wins Best Picture
events.description: The historical drama wins 6 Oscars at the 39th Academy Awards.

events.title: In the Heat of the Night Wins Best Picture
events.description: The crime drama starring Sidney Poitier wins 5 Oscars.

events.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey Released
events.description: Stanley Kubrick's sci-fi masterpiece revolutionizes visual effects and narrative.

events.title: Oliver! Wins Best Picture
events.description: The musical based on Charles Dickens' novel wins the top prize.

events.title: Midnight Cowboy Wins Best Picture
events.description: The only X-rated film to ever win Best Picture.

events.title: Patton Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: The war biopic wins Best Picture; George C. Scott famously refuses his Best Actor Oscar.

events.title: The French Connection Wins Best Picture
events.description: The gritty crime thriller wins 5 Oscars.

events.title: The Godfather Released
events.description: Francis Ford Coppola's masterpiece wins Best Picture and is considered one of the greatest films ever.

events.title: The Sting Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: The caper film starring Newman and Redford wins Best Picture.

events.title: The Godfather Part II Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first sequel to ever win Best Picture.

events.title: Jaws Released
events.description: Steven Spielberg's thriller creates the 'summer blockbuster' phenomenon.

events.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest Wins Big Five
events.description: The second film to win all five major Academy Awards.

events.title: Rocky Wins Best Picture
events.description: The underdog boxing drama wins the top prize over Taxi Driver and Network.

events.title: Star Wars Released
events.description: George Lucas' space epic revolutionizes special effects and becomes a global phenomenon.

events.title: Annie Hall Wins Best Picture
events.description: Woody Allen's romantic comedy wins over Star Wars.

events.title: The Deer Hunter Wins Best Picture
events.description: The intense Vietnam War drama wins 5 Oscars.

events.title: Kramer vs. Kramer Wins Best Picture
events.description: The divorce drama wins 5 Oscars at the 52nd Academy Awards.

events.title: Ordinary People Wins Best Picture
events.description: Robert Redford's directorial debut wins the top prize.

events.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark Released
events.description: Steven Spielberg and George Lucas collaborate to create the ultimate adventure hero, Indiana Jones.

events.title: Chariots of Fire Wins Best Picture
events.description: The British sports drama wins 4 Oscars.

events.title: Blade Runner Released
events.description: Ridley Scott's sci-fi noir becomes a cult classic and redefines 'cyberpunk' visuals.

events.title: Gandhi Wins 8 Oscars
events.description: The biographical epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: Terms of Endearment Wins Best Picture
events.description: The family drama wins 5 Oscars.

events.title: Amadeus Wins 8 Oscars
events.description: The biographical drama about Mozart wins Best Picture.

events.title: Out of Africa Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: The romantic drama starring Meryl Streep wins Best Picture.

events.title: Platoon Wins Best Picture
events.description: Oliver Stone's war drama wins 4 Oscars.

events.title: The Last Emperor Wins 9 Oscars
events.description: Bernardo Bertolucci's epic wins in every category it was nominated for.

events.title: Rain Man Wins Best Picture
events.description: The road drama starring Dustin Hoffman wins 4 Oscars.

events.title: Driving Miss Daisy Wins Best Picture
events.description: The comedy-drama wins 4 Oscars at the 62nd Academy Awards.

events.title: Dances with Wolves Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: Kevin Costner's Western epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: The Silence of the Lambs Wins Big Five
events.description: The third and most recent film to win all five major Oscars.

events.title: Unforgiven Wins Best Picture
events.description: Clint Eastwood's revisionist Western wins 4 Oscars.

events.title: Jurassic Park Released
events.description: Spielberg's dinosaur epic pioneers the use of CGI in film.

events.title: Schindler's List Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: Steven Spielberg's Holocaust drama wins Best Picture.

events.title: Forrest Gump Wins 6 Oscars
events.description: The drama starring Tom Hanks wins Best Picture.

events.title: Toy Story Released
events.description: Pixar releases the first feature-length computer-animated film.

events.title: Braveheart Wins 5 Oscars
events.description: Mel Gibson's historical epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: The English Patient Wins 9 Oscars
events.description: The romantic war drama wins Best Picture.

events.title: Titanic Wins 11 Oscars
events.description: James Cameron's epic ties the record for most wins and becomes the highest-grossing film of its time.

events.title: Shakespeare in Love Wins Best Picture
events.description: The romantic comedy-drama wins 7 Oscars over Saving Private Ryan.

events.title: The Matrix Released
events.description: The Wachowskis' sci-fi action film revolutionizes visual effects with 'bullet time'.

events.title: American Beauty Wins 5 Oscars
events.description: The drama directed by Sam Mendes wins Best Picture.

events.title: Gladiator Wins 5 Oscars
events.description: Ridley Scott's Roman epic wins Best Picture.

events.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon Released
events.description: Ang Lee's wuxia masterpiece brings the genre to global mainstream success.

events.title: A Beautiful Mind Wins 4 Oscars
events.description: The biographical drama about John Nash wins Best Picture.

events.title: Chicago Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first musical to win Best Picture since Oliver! in 1968.

events.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King Wins 11 Oscars
events.description: Peter Jackson's epic finale ties the record for most wins and sweeps all its nominations.

events.title: Million Dollar Baby Wins 4 Oscars
events.description: Clint Eastwood's boxing drama wins Best Picture.

events.title: Crash Wins Best Picture
events.description: The ensemble drama wins in a major upset over Brokeback Mountain.

events.title: The Departed Wins Best Picture
events.description: Martin Scorsese finally wins Best Director as his film takes the top prize.

events.title: No Country for Old Men Wins 4 Oscars
events.description: The Coen brothers' neo-Western wins Best Picture.

events.title: The Dark Knight Released
events.description: Christopher Nolan's superhero film receives universal acclaim and changes the genre's perception.

events.title: Slumdog Millionaire Wins 8 Oscars
events.description: Danny Boyle's drama set in Mumbai wins Best Picture.

events.title: Avatar Released
events.description: James Cameron's sci-fi epic revolutionizes 3D cinema and becomes the highest-grossing film of all time.

events.title: The Hurt Locker Wins Best Picture
events.description: Kathryn Bigelow becomes the first woman to win Best Director.

events.title: The King's Speech Wins 4 Oscars
events.description: The historical drama wins Best Picture.

events.title: The Artist Wins Best Picture
events.description: The silent, black-and-white film wins the top prize in the digital age.

events.title: Argo Wins Best Picture
events.description: Ben Affleck's thriller wins despite him missing a Best Director nomination.

events.title: 12 Years a Slave Wins Best Picture
events.description: Steve McQueen's powerful historical drama wins 3 Oscars.

events.title: Birdman Wins Best Picture
events.description: Alejandro G. Iñárritu's film, seemingly shot in one take, wins the top prize.

events.title: Spotlight Wins Best Picture
events.description: The investigative journalism drama wins 2 Oscars.

events.title: Moonlight Wins Best Picture
events.description: The film wins after a historic envelope mix-up at the 89th Academy Awards.

events.title: The Shape of Water Wins Best Picture
events.description: Guillermo del Toro's fantasy romance wins 4 Oscars.

events.title: Green Book Wins Best Picture
events.description: The biographical comedy-drama wins 3 Oscars.

events.title: Parasite Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first non-English language film to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.

events.title: Nomadland Wins Best Picture
events.description: Chloé Zhao wins Best Director, becoming the second woman and first woman of color to do so.

events.title: CODA Wins Best Picture
events.description: The first film released by a streaming service (Apple TV+) to win Best Picture.

events.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: The multiverse-spanning film wins Best Picture and breaks records for total awards won.

events.title: Oppenheimer Wins 7 Oscars
events.description: Christopher Nolan's biographical thriller wins Best Picture and Best Director.
